To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the most effective way to fuse data from multiple physiological sensors in order to determine psychological states is to first extract features that are relevant to the psychological states of interest, and then use a linear discriminant analysis to classify the data.
the most important factor that determines the success of data fusion is the choice of a good psychological model.

the following methods can be used to achieve data fusion in physiological computing: (1) the psychological model should be chosen based on the application, the training set should be collected using an experimental protocol that is similar to the application, the features should be extracted from the data, the features should then be normalized to a range of 0–1, and the number of features should be reduced by principal component analysis.

the development of an adaptive system that can learn from its user and adapt itself to his/her preferences and needs.
how to make the best use of the information that is available in the data.
the use of autonomic nervous system response measures as an input channel to computer interfaces.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

there is no universal method for data fusion and adaptation in physiological computing, but there are many different approaches that can be applied in various contexts, depending on the specific requirements of the system.
the current methods for data fusion are not yet mature enough to provide a universal solution.
, despite a vast number of studies and a great deal of work, there is still much to be done before we can say that physiological computing is ready for the mass market.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are able to detect the emotional states of users by using physiological signals.
the data fusion and system adaption using autonomic nervous systems is an active area of research in the physiological computing and psychophysiology.
the data fusion of autonomic nervous system data for physiological computing is still a challenging task and there are still a lot of open questions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the most successful approaches to data fusion and system adaptations are the ones that are based on the user’s individual characteristics.
the best approach to data fusion and system adaptations depends on the type of psychological states that the user is experiencing.
, in physiological computing, the choice of a feature extraction method is crucial, and the choice of a classification method is less so.
